contrary_evidence: Papers and long yields rallied on November 4 while latest euro-area flash inflation rose to 4.0% and US services prices diffusion remained 73.0; no established simultaneous disinflation.
Oil futures fell 8.67% but neither verified normalized Strait of Hormuz cargo deliveries nor signed final peace terms were evidenced.
Brazil's equities closed +1.23% before the post-close Copom decision; market rally cannot be attributed to the later unchanged Selic communiqué.
ADP +86k private jobs differ methodologically from official BLS payrolls expected November 6; ISM index 73.0 is not a 73% inflation rate.
Brazil Copom paused while Australia's RBA had raised rates to 4.85% and US Treasury yields fell; monetary decisions are country-specific.
Congressional Democratic control changes oversight and bargaining, not automatically executive military policy or passed appropriations.
limitations: Cutoff 5 November 2026 01:58 BRT, with market closes from November 4 only; no claim of later trading or official November 6 US jobs data.
Brent and WTI are dated futures settlements; physical cargo, freight and refiners have not been independently demonstrated as fully normalized.
Eurostat October HICP is flash estimate, not final released time series.
US Treasury yields are constant-maturity rates, not transaction quotes or Fed administered rates.
ADP private jobs and ISM survey diffusion indices are different measures and cannot be converted directly into BLS payroll or CPI inflation.
Copom's unanimous November 4 decision postdates B3 trading close; no contemporaneous domestic market reaction to the communiqué inferred.
Election result is observed; subsequent policy outcomes, cessation of hostilities and energy transmission are scenarios rather than established events.

en.title: Global Macro — Oil's collapse and Treasury relief do not erase persistent inflation or restrictive monetary policy
en.deck: Brent falls 8.67% to $94.62 and 10-year Treasuries ease to 4.90% after the US midterms, while euro-area inflation reaches 4.0%, US services prices remain high and Brazil holds Selic at 13.75%.
en.regime: Conditional financial decompression following the US congressional election with sharp crude-price relief and lower long yields, but persistent euro-area and US services price pressures and restrictive Brazilian monetary policy.
en.key_risk: Confusing geopolitically sensitive futures and a one-day market rally with verified physical oil normalization, durable disinflation or enacted fiscal policy.
